title: Wraps Chain
statement: Implement `solve(names)`. `names` is the decorator stack written top to bottom, the same order as `@` lines above a function. The top decorator is the first name. On a call, the outermost wrapper runs first, and that outermost wrapper is the bottom decorator in the source, because it was applied last. Return the names in the order they run on the way in: bottom of the source list first, ending with the top of the source list.
constraints: names[0] is the top decorator in source
Return the call order on the way in
hints: Decorators apply from the function upward, so the bottom source name is outermost.
The call enters the outermost wrapper first.
Reversing the source list is the call order.
editorial: Application order is bottom-up. Call order on the way in is outside-in, which is the reverse of the source list when index 0 is the top line. Forgetting the reverse is the usual explanation of a trace that prints the inner wrapper first.
